newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C Amatil and San Miguel to merge soft drinks.
newsitem.headline: C-C Amatil and San Miguel to merge soft drinks.

text.p: Australian beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil said on Thursday it had agreed a A$3.4 billion ($2.7 billion) deal with San Miguel of the Philippines to create the largest Coca-Cola bottler outside the United States.

Under the agreement, Coca-Cola Amatil will issue 293 million shares to acquire San Miguel subsidiary Coca Cola Bottler Philippines (CCBPI), owned 70 percent by San Miguel and 30 percent by The Cola Cola Co of the U.S.
San Miguel would end up with a 25 percent stake in Coca-Cola Amatil, while The Coca Cola Co would see its shareholding in the Australian group diluted slightly to 33 percent.
Coca-Cola Amatil chairman Dean Wills said the merger was expected to be completed by mid-1997.
"The prospect of the expansion of Coca-Cola Amatil's interests into another major market in Asia is an exciting opportunity," Wills told shareholders at the firm's annual general meeting.

San Miguel chairman and chief executive officer Andres Soriano said in a statement that the move allowed San Miguel, the Philippines' largest beverage, food and packaging company, to expand the horizon of its soft drinks business.
The San Miguel subsidiary CCBPI owns and operates 21 soft drinks plants in the Philippines and has a 75 percent share of the Philippines market.
The company generated a net profit in 1996 of A$144 million, compared with Coca-Cola Amatil's 1996 net profit of A$142 million.

Coca-Cola Amatil already operates in 17 countries in the Asia-Pacific region and in Europe, mainly in eastern Europe. It has long vied with Mexico's Panamco for the status of being the largest Coca-Cola bottler outside of the United States.
News of the merger deal sent Coca-Cola Amatil shares soaring. In afternoon trade they were up 95 cents or 7.9 percent to A$12.90.
